# Baruch Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** She — Wisdom — is the book of God's commandments, the law that lasts forever. Hold on to her and you will live. Let her go and you will die.

**2** Come back, Jacob. Take hold of her. Walk toward her light, toward the brightness of her flames.

**3** Do not give what is glorious about you to another nation. Do not hand your gifts over to a foreign people.

**4** We are blessed, O Israel — because we know what God asks of us.

**5** Courage, my people! You are the living memory of Israel.

**6** You were sold off to the nations — but not to be destroyed. You were handed over to your enemies because you pushed God to anger.

**7** You provoked the one who made you. You offered sacrifice to demons instead of to God.

**8** You forgot the Eternal God who fed you and raised you. You broke the heart of Jerusalem, who nursed you like a mother.

**9** Jerusalem saw the wrath God was sending on you, and she spoke: Listen, you neighbors of Zion. God has laid a heavy grief on me.

**10** I watched my sons and daughters taken captive. The Eternal brought this on them.

**11** I raised them with such joy. I sent them away with nothing but weeping and sorrow.

**12** Do not pity me — I am a widow now, abandoned by so many. I sit here desolate because my children sinned, because they turned away from God's law,

**13** because they never learned his decrees, never walked in his commandments, never followed the paths of discipline his righteousness requires.

**14** Come, neighbors of Zion, come close. Remember my sons and daughters in their captivity — the Eternal brought this on them.

**15** He brought a nation against them from the ends of the earth — a brutal nation with a foreign tongue that had no respect for the elderly and no pity for children.

**16** That nation tore away the widow's beloved sons. They left her utterly alone, without even her daughters.

**17** What can I do for you? There is nothing I can do.

**18** The one who brought all this disaster upon you — he is the one who will rescue you from your enemies' grip.

**19** Go, my children. Go on your way. I am left here alone.

**20** I have taken off my robe of peace. I am wearing sackcloth now, crying out to the Eternal every day of my life.

**21** Be brave, my children. Cry out to God. He will rescue you from the power and the fist of the enemy.

**22** My hope for your salvation rests in the Eternal. Joy has already begun to stir in me because of the Holy One — because mercy is coming to you soon, from the one who saves you forever.

**23** I sent you away with grief and tears. God will bring you back to me in joy and gladness that will never end.

**24** The neighbors of Zion watched your captivity with their own eyes. Soon they will watch your salvation — the salvation God brings you, blazing with glory, radiant with the splendor of the Eternal.

**25** My children — bear it. Bear the anger God has sent upon you. Your enemy has run you down, but soon you will watch his ruin. You will put your foot on their necks.

**26** My tender children walked roads that were never meant for them, carried off like a flock stolen by raiders.

**27** Be brave, my children, and cry out to God. The one who sent this suffering will remember you.

**28** You chose to wander from God — now choose to come back. Put ten times the energy into seeking him as you put into leaving him.

**29** The one who brought all this trouble on you will bring you joy that lasts forever, together with your salvation.

**30** Courage, Jerusalem. The one who named you will comfort you.

**31** A curse on those who tormented you, who gloated when you fell.

**32** A curse on the cities your children were forced to serve. A curse on the city that swallowed your sons.

**33** She laughed at your ruin and celebrated your fall — she will mourn her own desolation when her turn comes.

**34** I will strip the pride out of her teeming city. All that boasting will turn to weeping.

**35** The Eternal will send fire upon her for many days, and for ages she will be a place haunted by demons.

**36** Jerusalem, look east! See the joy God is sending to you!

**37** Here they come — your children, the ones you sent away. They are coming from every direction, east and west alike, called home by the word of the Holy One, full of joy in the glory of God.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The maternal grief of Jerusalem in this chapter is one of the most moving passages in the Deuterocanon, and it anticipates the personification of Zion found in Lamentations and echoed in later Christian tradition (Mary at the cross, Rachel weeping in Matt 2:18). The rhythm of the mother's speech has been rendered to reflect the natural movements of grief: first her appeal to the neighbors (vv.9-14), then her helpless confession (vv.17-20), then a turn toward hope (vv.21-24), and finally her words of encouragement to her children (vv.25-29). The three-fold "take courage / be brave" (vv.5, 21, 27) forms a structural heartbeat of the chapter.*
